zh.title: 日本航空通勤ATR 72客機鹿兒島起飛後操縱指示異常折返平安降落
zh.summary: 日本航空通勤ATR 72-212A客機11月22日由鹿兒島飛往屋久島，爬升中機組接獲正副駕駛操縱桿動作不同步的警示，於1萬英尺停止爬升折返鹿兒島，約45分鐘後平安降落，機上48人無人受傷；航空公司表示未發現故障，飛機留場接受維修檢查。
body: 日本航空通勤ATR 72-212A客機、機身編號JA08JC，11月22日執行JL-3741航班由鹿兒島飛往屋久島，機上共有48人。客機由鹿兒島34號跑道起飛爬升時，機組接獲指示，指正駕駛與副駕駛的操縱桿動作並未同步，雖然兩側操縱桿看似同步移動。機組決定於1萬英尺停止爬升並折返鹿兒島，約45分鐘後平安降落。
航空公司表示，機組接獲警示，指正副駕駛的操縱桿動作不同步；雖然並未發現故障，飛機仍折返鹿兒島接受維修檢查。事件發生約16小時後，該機仍停留在鹿兒島地面。

en.title: JAC ATR 72 returns to Kagoshima after flight-control indication on climb
en.summary: A Japan Air Commuter ATR 72-212A operating flight JL-3741 from Kagoshima to Yakushima returned to Kagoshima on November 22 after the crew received an indication that the captain's and first officer's yokes were not moving in synchronisation. The aircraft landed safely about 45 minutes after departure with 48 people on board; the airline said no malfunction was found and the aircraft stayed on the ground for maintenance inspection.
body: A Japan Air Commuter ATR 72-212A, registration JA08JC, operating flight JL-3741 from Kagoshima to Yakushima in Japan with 48 people on board, was climbing out of Kagoshima's runway 34 when the crew received an indication that the yokes of the captain and first officer were not moving in synchronisation, although the yokes appeared to move in synchronisation. The crew stopped the climb at 10,000 feet and returned to Kagoshima, landing safely about 45 minutes after departure.

The airline reported that the crew had received an alert indicating that the captain's and first officer's control sticks were not moving in synchronisation. Although there was no malfunction, the aircraft returned to Kagoshima for inspection by maintenance. The aircraft was still on the ground in Kagoshima about 16 hours after landing.

facts.claim: Japan Air Commuter ATR 72-212A JA08JC operated flight JL-3741 from Kagoshima to Yakushima with 48 people on board.
While climbing out of runway 34, the crew received an indication that the captain's and first officer's yokes were not moving in synchronisation.
The crew stopped the climb at 10,000 feet and returned to Kagoshima, landing safely about 45 minutes after departure.
The airline reported the alert and said no malfunction was found; the aircraft returned for maintenance inspection and was still on the ground about 16 hours after landing.
